This paper examines the emerging field of responsible AI systems, in which (algorithmic decision-making [data governance {ethical constraints [social impact assessment {accountability mechanisms}]}]}) functions as both a technical and institutional design challenge. We argue that evaluating AI requires nested scrutiny—spanning (models [datasets {training objectives [deployment contexts {sociotechnical feedback loops}]}]})—and we propose a multidisciplinary framework for assessing transparency, fairness, and resilience.
